_topics: One pipeline's answer, not a rule. What the topics are follows from the business case in the interview; what the HARNESS needs is only this much: topics.in is the one topic it fills and measures, and every topic in topics.out must grow by a constant multiple of it. Everything else is the pipeline's business. The interview's default business case also has a prices input keyed by symbol and a market-values output emitted every 10 seconds; both are the project's, which is why they are absent here rather than forbidden. Create and fill the price topic yourself (the generator is the natural place: fill it once at build time, it is tens of records, not millions) and read it as a second source. Write market values to their own topic and keep it OUT of topics.out: its rows are per interval, not per input, so counting them would make the two vantage points disagree by construction. Set retention.bytes on both, since the harness will not (section 3).
_marketValues: The throttled emit the interview asks for. Configurable interval, default 10000 ms. It is not counted in outputsPerInput and its topic is not in topics.out — see _topics. The verifier should still check it: every market value equal to that key's final position x its latest published price, exactly, which is one of the assertions section 4 requires.
_outputsPerInput: Sink records per input record, summed across every output topic. Derive it, do not copy this: the two-vantage guard compares broker offsets against sink rows and a wrong value makes them disagree. One position per trade plus one per allocation at four allocations is 1 + 4 = 5, not 8.
_cases: The cases the suite measures, and the steps it reports: 1->2 and 2->4. The one-core case is measured, not assumed -- six recorded suites returned 1.978-2.161x on 1->2, so a healthy baseline sits on the ideal 2.00x. A 1->2 well above that means the one-core case under-read, and the tiny proof bounds every one of these steps before the suite is spent.

backlog._count: The suite drains this at every case. Size it with the same rule the tiny proof checks: the fastest case's rate x (warm-up ceiling + window + two checkpoint intervals). Shipped at 160,000,000, it was short at every rate this rig has produced -- 199,832,940 needed at run 31's measured 740,122/s -- and a short suite backlog costs the suite, not the tiny proof. 275,000,000 covers the fastest rate on record (964,913/s, run 15) and costs a few minutes more fill.
backlog._tinyCount: The tiny proof drains this. Size it for the warm-up ceiling plus the window plus two checkpoint intervals at the fastest case's rate -- 120 + 40 + 20 s. Guess high: a wrong guess costs one tiny proof, and too small costs the chain. Clean-room runs 30 and 31 both needed 150,000,000; run 32 shipped with 60,000,000, which held 94 s at the rate its 4-core case read, against a 55 s warm-up, and neither tiny case could settle. 175,000,000 covers the fastest rate on record.
backlog._killAtFraction: Approximate by construction: offsets commit once per checkpoint interval, so the kill lands at the first commit past this fraction. Clean-room run 30 asked for 0.35 and it landed at 62.7%, while the log still said 35%.

_caps: tmMemoryBase + tmMemoryPerCore x cores gives every subtask the same memory: 1728m at 1 core, 2368m at 2, 3648m at 4. Leaving them out does not leave memory to the engine -- the image ships config.yaml with taskmanager.memory.process.size: 1728m, so every case would get the same flat figure, which is the configuration preflight refuses. Clean-room run 36 measured it: 2->4 read 1.510 on the image default and 1.743 with these values. Kafka's memory is the setting that most often costs a suite. What matters is kafkaMemory minus kafkaHeap -- the rest is page cache, and a broker that cannot cache the backlog reads it back off disk and becomes the constraint. Every configuration in record/configs.json that produced a usable table left 4.25-5.00 GB; these values leave 5.00 GB and are the pair behind the best recorded result (2->4 = 2.114x).
_flinkProperties: Extra Flink settings for the job manager and every task manager. A metrics reporter goes here -- section 7 wants panels that need one. Example: {"metrics.reporter.prom.factory.class": "org.apache.flink.metrics.prometheus.PrometheusReporterFactory", "metrics.reporter.prom.port": "9249"} with the prometheus jar in the image's plugins directory. Slots, parallelism, worker memory, the checkpoint store and metrics.reporter.slf4j.* are refused: they decide what is being measured.

Extra Flink settings for the job manager and every task manager. env.java.opts.taskmanager pins the garbage collector, and it is not optional: --cpus 1 makes the JVM see one processor and choose the serial collector, while every other case gets G1. Clean-room run 35 measured it -- pinning G1 gave the one-core case +19% and moved 1->2 from 2.364x to 1.997x, so the whole superlinear first step had been the baseline running different code. A metrics reporter goes here too. Slots, parallelism, memory, the checkpoint store and metrics.reporter.slf4j.* are refused: they decide what is being measured.
_keySets: Which manifest fields hold a keyed stage's key set. Preflight asks Flink's own
key-group assignment, out of the image under test, where each key would land at
every case's parallelism. Four keys do not spread over four subtasks by
themselves: the demo's sixteen account keys land 5/3/4/4 at Flink's default
maxParallelism of 128, so one core would do a quarter more work than an even
split and that stage could not return more than 0.80 of linear at four cores.
When that happens the preflight row names the pipeline.max-parallelism to add
below -- for these key names it is 1115 -- and the layout becomes 4/4/4/4.
axis: one worker growing: one task manager container capped at N cores, parallelism N, N slots
apiLevel: Flink DataStream API, hand-written operators (no SQL, no Table API)

guarantee.sink: at-least-once, idempotent by emitting the absolute position per key

_images: Apache is the default. For Confluent set kafka to confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.7.0 and kafkaLibs to /usr/share/java/kafka -- the harness mines the broker image for its kafka-clients jar and runs the offset sampler inside it, so the library path moves with the vendor.
